passage:
Monday: Boxes crowded the hall, and Farhan, nearly two, would not leave his father Suraj's leg. He carried his stitched blue elephant everywhere.
Thursday: In the new flat the walls echoed. Farhan sat on the bare floor, elephant under his chin, and cried when Suraj stepped into the next room. Suraj set the elephant's blanket and Farhan's cup by the window.
Sunday: Farhan pointed at a crow from the balcony and toddled five steps alone, elephant under his arm.

qa.q: What did Farhan carry everywhere?
qa.a: He carried his stitched blue elephant.

qa.q: What was Farhan feeling in the echoing new flat?
qa.a: He was scared and unsettled, shown by how he cried whenever Suraj stepped into the next room.

qa.q: What did Suraj do that helped Farhan settle?
qa.a: Suraj set the elephant's blanket and Farhan's cup by the window, so familiar things were in view in the strange place.

qa.q: How might Suraj have felt while Farhan clung to his leg during the packing?
qa.a: Suraj was probably tired and busy with the move but also tender, since he stayed close and made room for the familiar things.

grounding: A toddler in a relocating family clings more, and familiar objects and routines give security in the new place.

passage: Vikas, two and a half, followed his mother through the Pune flat, a fist wound in her dupatta. Taped boxes stood in the hall, and Jatin argued with the movers on the phone. When Mummy knelt to tape another, Vikas climbed into her lap. She found his red steel bowl and yellow rattle in the open bag and hummed his nap-time lullaby. His shoulders dropped. He put the rattle in the bowl, then his head on her arm.

qa.q: How did Vikas stay close to his mother as she moved through the flat?
qa.a: He kept a fist wound in her dupatta.

qa.q: Why did Vikas climb into Mummy's lap?
qa.a: He was feeling anxious among the taped boxes and the busy adults, so he wanted the safety of his mother's closeness.

qa.q: What helped Vikas relax, and what small step could the family repeat in the new flat?
qa.a: His red steel bowl, yellow rattle and the usual lullaby helped him relax; unpacking those and singing at nap time could keep giving him a familiar routine.

qa.q: What might Jatin's phone argument mean for how the day feels to Vikas?
qa.a: The raised voice of Jatin with the movers adds to the stress in the flat, so Vikas may pick up on the tension even without understanding the words.

grounding: A toddler in a relocating family clings to his mother, and familiar objects and a lullaby give security.

passage:
Monday. Boxes filled the flat. Irfan, two, climbed into an empty one and would not come out.
Wednesday. Ammi and Abbu spoke in tight voices. Irfan clung to Ammi's leg and cried when Rajni Aunty, the neighbour, tried to pick him up.
Saturday. In the new flat in Hyderabad, everything smelled strange. Irfan wailed at bedtime. Ammi dug through a box and found his blue blanket and the old lullaby.
He sucked his thumb, held the blanket's corner, and slept.

qa.q: What did Ammi find in the box?
qa.a: She found his blue blanket and the old lullaby.

qa.q: Why did Irfan cling to Ammi's leg?
qa.a: Irfan felt unsettled and scared by the boxes and the adults' tight voices, so he wanted to stay close to Ammi.

qa.q: What helped Irfan settle in the new flat?
qa.a: His familiar blue blanket and the old lullaby gave him a sense of security in a strange place.

qa.q: What might the move be like for Ammi?
qa.a: Ammi is probably stressed and tired, but she notices what Irfan needs and finds his comforts.

grounding: A toddler notices the boxes and stressed adults during a move, clings more, and settles with familiar objects and routines.

passage:
The movers came at seven. Nikita, two, watched her toys vanish into cartons and started to wail. She clung to Salma Didi, the nanny, and wouldn't let go.
In the new flat in Delhi, nothing was familiar. Nikita refused her food and followed Mumma from room to room.
That night, Salma Didi unpacked the small plastic plate with ducks and the orange cup first, and hummed the usual bath song. Nikita ate every bite from the duck plate.

qa.q: What did Salma Didi unpack first?
qa.a: She unpacked the small plastic plate with ducks and the orange cup first.

qa.q: How was Nikita feeling when she followed Mumma from room to room?
qa.a: Nikita felt insecure and anxious in the strange new flat, wanting to stay close.

qa.q: Why did the duck plate and the bath song help?
qa.a: Familiar objects and routines made the new place feel safer, so Nikita could relax and eat.

qa.q: How might Salma Didi feel when Nikita eats every bite?
qa.a: Salma Didi would probably feel relieved and pleased that the familiar things worked.

grounding: A toddler in a relocating family is upset by packing and clings more, and familiar objects and routines give her security.

passage:
"Yusuf, come, we're going on the big plane!"
"No!" Yusuf gripped the doorframe.
"Maria, he's been clingy all week," Papa said. "All these boxes."
"He can feel we're stressed," Mama said. "Yusuf, where's Bunny?"
"Bunny!" He ran and grabbed the grey rabbit.
On the plane he held Bunny tight. At the new house, Mama sang the same song as every night.
"Bunny sleep," Yusuf said, and lay down.

qa.q: What was the name of Yusuf's toy?
qa.a: The grey rabbit was called Bunny.

qa.q: Why was Yusuf clingy all week?
qa.a: Yusuf felt uneasy and insecure because of the boxes and the adults' stress.

qa.q: What could other parents learn from Mama?
qa.a: Keep a favourite toy close and repeat the usual bedtime song, so a toddler feels secure in a new place.

qa.q: How might Papa be feeling during the move?
qa.a: Papa seems tired and worried, noticing that Yusuf has been clingy all week.

grounding: A toddler senses the stress of a family move and clings more, and a favourite toy and familiar bedtime song help him feel secure.

passage:
Daycare note, Tuesday. Yamini, room teacher.
Nilesh arrived clinging to his mother's dupatta and would not let go for twenty minutes. She said they are packing for the move to Pune and the flat is full of boxes. He cried when I took his blue bottle to wash, so I gave it straight back. He settled once he had the bottle and his usual song at nap time. What I did next: asked his mother to pack his bedsheet and bottle last, and unpack them first.

qa.q: What made Nilesh cry at daycare?
qa.a: He cried when his blue bottle was taken to wash.

qa.q: Why was Nilesh clinging to his mother's dupatta?
qa.a: He was probably anxious and unsettled by the boxes and the move, and wanted to stay close to someone familiar.

qa.q: Why was packing the bedsheet and bottle last a good idea?
qa.a: Those familiar things will be the first ones out in the new flat, giving Nilesh a sense of security in a strange place.

qa.q: What might the move feel like for Nilesh's mother?
qa.a: She is probably busy and a little stressed with the packing, and may feel relieved to have a simple plan to help him settle.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler clinging more during a family move and how familiar objects and routines give him security.
